intervention_label: SMARCB1/INI1 expression across uterine mesenchymal tumours
model_system: human surgical specimens, 206 uterine mesenchymal tumours (170 smooth-muscle tumours) by IHC
control_arm: internal non-neoplastic stroma/endothelium as staining control
mechanism: INI1 protein readout of SMARCB1 status in the exact anatomic lineage in question
key_finding: Every one of the 206 uterine mesenchymal tumours retained SMARCB1 expression, including all 170 smooth-muscle tumours. Two tumours lost SMARCA4/SMARCA2, and neither was a leiomyosarcoma.
caveats: Single-institution Japanese cohort scored by IHC alone, so a subclonal or metastasis-restricted SMARCB1 event would not be captured. This is the hardest available prior against INI1 loss in this histology and it is a prior, not a result for this patient.

intervention_label: Snf5 heterozygous mice — allele dosage and rhabdoid tumour onset
journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
model_system: germline Snf5 knockout mouse (heterozygous and homozygous)
control_arm: wild-type littermates
mechanism: genetic test of how many SMARCB1 alleles must be lost before the rhabdoid phenotype appears
key_finding: Homozygous Snf5 null embryos died by embryonic day 7, while heterozygotes were born normal and only later developed focal rhabdoid-like tumours from about 5 weeks of age. One inactivated allele was therefore compatible with normal tissue, and tumours arose focally rather than across the whole heterozygous animal.
caveats: Mouse germline model of a paediatric rhabdoid phenotype; the tumours arise from first-branchial-arch soft tissue, not myometrium. Bears on this case only through the allele-dosage question.

intervention_label: Ini1 heterozygous mice — second-hit requirement (LOH) for tumour formation
model_system: germline Ini1 knockout mouse; tumours from heterozygotes genotyped at the Ini1 locus
control_arm: wild-type and untransformed heterozygous tissue
mechanism: loss of the remaining wild-type allele as the rate-limiting event downstream of a single inactivating hit
key_finding: About 15% of Ini1-heterozygous mice developed mostly undifferentiated sarcomas, and tumour formation went along with loss of heterozygosity at the Ini1 locus. Ini1-null embryos died between 3.5 and 5.5 days post-coitum.
caveats: This is the paper that makes the mono- versus bi-allelic distinction concrete: a single truncating allele was not the transformed state, LOH was. Mouse germline model, undifferentiated sarcoma rather than smooth muscle.

intervention_label: SMARCB1 as the BAF subunit required for enhancer activation
model_system: SMARCB1-deficient rhabdoid cell lines with inducible SMARCB1 re-expression; ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq
control_arm: isogenic SMARCB1 re-expressing cells
mechanism: SMARCB1 loss collapses BAF occupancy and remodelling at typical enhancers while residual complex persists at super-enhancers
key_finding: Re-expressing SMARCB1 restored BAF binding and accessibility at thousands of typical enhancers and at bivalent promoters. The residual SMARCB1-less complex retained super-enhancer occupancy, which explains why loss of this one subunit reprograms rather than abolishes BAF function.
caveats: Isogenic rhabdoid systems only; no smooth-muscle or mesenchymal-lineage cells tested. Supports why complete INI1 protein loss, not a heterozygous variant call, is the biologically meaningful state.

intervention_label: Conditional Snf5 inversion — tumour spectrum after biallelic loss
exclusion_reason: The tumour spectrum after conditional biallelic Snf5 loss was mature CD8+ T-cell lymphoma with only rare rhabdoid tumours, so the model speaks to lymphoid rather than mesenchymal transformation; the allele configuration is also biallelic, which is not the patient's called genotype.

intervention_label: Snf5 loss drives EZH2 dependence — genetic proof
model_system: conditional Snf5 mouse crossed to conditional Ezh2; SNF5-deficient MEFs and human rhabdoid tumours
control_arm: Snf5-loss animals with intact Ezh2
mechanism: SNF5 loss raises EZH2 and drives H3K27me3 across Polycomb targets; the two complexes act antagonistically on stem-cell programs
key_finding: Polycomb targets were broadly trimethylated and repressed in SNF5-deficient cells, and inactivating Ezh2 genetically blocked tumour formation driven by Snf5 loss. The dependency is genetic, not merely correlative.
caveats: Whole rationale rests on complete Snf5 loss in a mouse rhabdoid context. Nothing here tests a smooth-muscle lineage or a heterozygous truncating allele. An erratum was published (Cancer Cell 2011;19:153).

intervention_label: EPZ-6438 (tazemetostat) in SMARCB1-deleted rhabdoid tumours
journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
model_system: SMARCB1-deleted malignant rhabdoid tumour cell lines and subcutaneous xenografts in mice
control_arm: vehicle-treated xenografts; SMARCB1-wild-type lines as the specificity comparator
dose_and_schedule: oral, dose-ranging; intratumoural H3K27me3 measured as the pharmacodynamic readout
mechanism: selective inhibition of EZH2 methyltransferase activity, lowering H3K27me3 and releasing differentiation programs in SMARCB1-null cells
key_finding: Apoptosis and differentiation followed EZH2 inhibition specifically in SMARCB1-deleted rhabdoid lines. Xenografts regressed dose-dependently with matching loss of intratumoural H3K27me3, and tumours did not regrow after dosing stopped.
caveats: This is the origin of the whole SMARCB1-to-EZH2 therapeutic logic, and every model in it is a paediatric rhabdoid tumour with biallelic SMARCB1 deletion. All authors but one were Epizyme employees.

intervention_label: EZH2 dependency in SWI/SNF-mutant cancers is largely non-catalytic
model_system: panel of cancer cell lines and xenografts mutant for ARID1A, PBRM1 or SMARCA4; shRNA/CRISPR versus enzymatic inhibitor
control_arm: SWI/SNF-wild-type lines; catalytically dead and stabilisation-competent EZH2 rescue constructs
mechanism: EZH2 supports PRC2 complex stability independently of its methyltransferase activity, so genetic depletion and enzymatic inhibition are not equivalent
key_finding: EZH2 was essential across the SWI/SNF-mutant lines tested, but the dependency ran mostly through a non-catalytic stabilising role, with only partial reliance on methyltransferase activity. A co-occurring Ras-pathway mutation abrogated the dependency altogether.
caveats: The mutant subunits tested were ARID1A, PBRM1 and SMARCA4, not SMARCB1. The practical warning for this case is that an enzymatic EZH2 inhibitor may under-deliver even where the genetic dependency is real.

intervention_label: EZH2 inhibition versus conventional chemotherapy in an INI1-negative epithelioid sarcoma PDX
model_system: INI1-deficient proximal-type epithelioid sarcoma patient-derived xenograft (PDX ES-1) and the derived ES-1 cell line
control_arm: untreated mice; doxorubicin, ifosfamide, doxorubicin+ifosfamide and gemcitabine arms
dose_and_schedule: EPZ-011989 versus doxorubicin, ifosfamide, the doxorubicin-ifosfamide doublet, and gemcitabine
mechanism: EZH2 methyltransferase inhibition in a tumour with complete INI1 loss, with autophagy induction as the escape route
key_finding: Maximum tumour volume inhibition of roughly 90% was reached by gemcitabine, by EPZ-011989 and by doxorubicin plus ifosfamide alike. RNA-seq and functional work on residual tumour pointed to autophagy, with HMGA2 central, as a cytoprotective response to EZH2 inhibition.
caveats: One PDX from one INI1-negative epithelioid sarcoma. EZH2 inhibition matched rather than beat anthracycline-based chemotherapy in this model, which is worth holding next to any cross-histology extrapolation.

intervention_label: EZH2 protein levels in leiomyosarcoma versus leiomyoma
model_system: human myogenic tumour specimens by IHC (leiomyosarcoma vs leiomyoma, rhabdomyosarcoma vs rhabdomyoma) with GEO expression datasets
control_arm: benign myogenic counterparts
mechanism: PRC2 subunit expression as a correlate of malignancy in smooth-muscle tumours
key_finding: EZH2 protein was high in leiomyosarcoma and low or absent in leiomyoma, with SUZ12 and EED following a weaker version of the same pattern.
caveats: Expression is not dependency. High EZH2 in an INI1-intact smooth-muscle tumour is a proliferation correlate, and none of these tumours were tested against an EZH2 inhibitor.

intervention_label: EZH1/2 dual inhibitors (valemetostat chemical series) — antitumor profile and SWI/SNF correlation
model_system: haematological and solid cancer cell-line panels plus DLBCL xenografts; 14-day rat tolerability
control_arm: EZH2-selective inhibitor as the head-to-head comparator; vehicle
dose_and_schedule: orally bioavailable EZH1/2 dual inhibitors, once-daily oral dosing in vivo
mechanism: simultaneous inhibition of EZH1- and EZH2-containing PRC2 suppresses H3K27me3 more completely than EZH2-selective blockade
key_finding: Dual EZH1/2 inhibition dropped H3K27me3 further and outperformed the EZH2-selective comparator in EZH2 gain-of-function DLBCL in vitro and in vivo. Across the solid-tumour panel the authors found no clear correlation between sensitivity and SWI/SNF mutation status, with few exceptions.
caveats: The absent SWI/SNF-sensitivity correlation cuts against using a SMARCB1 call as the selection biomarker for this class. No sarcoma or smooth-muscle model appears in the panel, and the compounds are the chemical series behind valemetostat rather than the clinical agent itself.

intervention_label: ncBAF/BRD9 as a synthetic-lethal target in BAF-perturbed cancers
model_system: synovial sarcoma and malignant rhabdoid tumour cell lines; chemical (BRD9 degrader/inhibitor) and shRNA depletion; genome-wide complex mapping
control_arm: cBAF-intact cancer lines; non-targeting constructs
mechanism: ncBAF complexes localise to CTCF sites and promoters and sustain gene expression when cBAF is crippled by SMARCB1 loss or SS18-SSX fusion
key_finding: Depleting BRD9 rapidly cut proliferation of synovial sarcoma and rhabdoid lines but spared cBAF-intact cancers. The surviving dependency in SMARCB1-perturbed cells ran through ncBAF maintenance of retained CTCF-promoter sites.
caveats: Cell-line dependency mapping with limited in-vivo work; both index histologies carry complete cBAF perturbation. This is the rationale that sent FHD-609 and CFT8634 into the clinic, and both programmes were later discontinued.

intervention_label: BRD9 vulnerability in SMARCB1-mutant rhabdoid tumours and why the bromodomain is the wrong handle
model_system: genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 screen across cancer lines with follow-up in SMARCB1-mutant rhabdoid tumour lines
control_arm: SMARCB1-wild-type lines; domain-deletion BRD9 rescue constructs
mechanism: SMARCB1 loss increases BRD9 incorporation into a distinct SWI/SNF sub-complex whose integrity depends on the DUF3512 domain
key_finding: BRD9 scored as a specific dependency in rhabdoid tumours, and SMARCB1 loss itself drove more BRD9 into the complex. The bromodomain was dispensable while DUF3512 was essential, which is the mechanistic argument for degrading BRD9 rather than inhibiting its bromodomain.
caveats: Paediatric rhabdoid lines with biallelic SMARCB1 loss throughout; nothing on heterozygous alleles or mesenchymal smooth-muscle lineage. An erratum was published (Nat Commun 2019;10:4445).

intervention_label: dBRD9 degradation reverses the oncogenic program in synovial sarcoma
model_system: synovial sarcoma cell lines treated with the BRD9 degrader dBRD9; proteomics and expression profiling
control_arm: bromodomain-inhibitor comparator and non-SS18-SSX lines
mechanism: targeted degradation removes BRD9 protein and the ncBAF assembly it scaffolds, undoing SS18-SSX-driven transcription
key_finding: Degrading BRD9 reversed the oncogenic expression program and suppressed synovial sarcoma growth, where bromodomain occupancy alone was insufficient.
caveats: Synovial sarcoma is driven by SS18-SSX-mediated SMARCB1 ejection, a different route to the same complex defect than a SMARCB1 mutation; largely in-vitro.

intervention_label: BRD9 in androgen-receptor signalling and prostate cancer
exclusion_reason: BRD9 dependency here is androgen-receptor-driven in prostate epithelium, not a consequence of cBAF perturbation, so the mechanism diverges from the SMARCB1-loss rationale that is at issue in this case.

intervention_label: Uterine sarcoma patient-derived xenograft panel — engraftment and fidelity
model_system: subcutaneous patient-derived xenografts from uterine sarcoma and carcinosarcoma in immunocompromised mice
n_units: 13 LMS implanted, 10 engrafted (77%); 2/7 carcinosarcoma (29%); 1 high-grade uterine sarcoma NOS
control_arm: paired original patient tumour for histology, copy-number and RNA comparison
mechanism: not applicable — model characterisation
key_finding: Leiomyosarcoma engrafted at 77% and the xenografts looked histologically like their source tumours, with desmin or h-caldesmon retained in 8 of 10. Copy-number concordance with the parent tumour ranged from 57.7% to 98.2%, and three LMS models clustered away from their originating tumour by RNA expression.
caveats: Subcutaneous rather than orthotopic, immunodeficient hosts, and the RNA drift in three of ten LMS models is the honest limit on how far a uLMS PDX result travels. This is close to the whole published uLMS PDX resource.

intervention_label: Leiomyosarcoma genomic and transcriptomic landscape
model_system: human leiomyosarcoma tumours profiled by whole-exome/genome and RNA sequencing, with functional follow-up in LMS cell lines
control_arm: normal tissue comparators for somatic calling
mechanism: recurrent inactivation of TP53, RB1 and PTEN with widespread copy-number change; telomere maintenance and DNA-damage-response features rather than a single driver oncogene
key_finding: Leiomyosarcoma is copy-number driven, with TP53 and RB1 loss recurring and few actionable point mutations. Telomere-maintenance and homologous-recombination features stood out as the recurring biology.
caveats: Mixed anatomic sites rather than uterus-only. Sets the expectation that a TP53 nonsense call in this histology is background biology rather than a lead.

intervention_label: Exome landscape of uterine leiomyosarcoma — TP53, ATRX, MED12
model_system: whole-exome sequencing of uterine leiomyosarcoma specimens with matched normal DNA
control_arm: matched germline DNA
mechanism: defines which genes are recurrently hit in this specific histology
key_finding: TP53, ATRX and MED12 were the recurrently mutated genes in uterine leiomyosarcoma. SMARCB1 was not among the recurrent events.
caveats: Descriptive sequencing with no therapeutic arm. Useful mainly as the denominator against which the plasma SMARCB1 call should be judged.

intervention_label: MYOCD amplification as a lineage dependency in leiomyosarcoma
model_system: human retroperitoneal leiomyosarcoma series with siRNA knockdown in LMS cell lines
control_arm: non-targeting siRNA; non-amplified tumours
mechanism: myocardin amplification sustains the smooth-muscle transcriptional program that defines the lineage
key_finding: MYOCD was amplified and overexpressed in most well-differentiated retroperitoneal leiomyosarcomas, and knocking it down reduced smooth-muscle marker expression and proliferation.
caveats: Retroperitoneal rather than uterine LMS, and no drug exists against myocardin. Included because lineage dependency is the alternative frame to the borrowed epigenetic one.

intervention_label: Conditional p53/BRCA1 deletion in the murine uterus — a uLMS model and human BRCA1 loss
model_system: Amhr2-Cre conditional p53 and p53/BRCA1 deleted mice; human uterine leiomyosarcoma specimens for BRCA1 protein and promoter methylation
control_arm: p53-deleted-only animals; BRCA1-intact human tumours
mechanism: p53 loss initiates uterine smooth-muscle tumours and concurrent BRCA1 loss accelerates them, with promoter methylation as the human silencing route
key_finding: Conditional p53 deletion produced uterine tumours resembling human uLMS, and adding BRCA1 deletion accelerated progression. BRCA1 protein was absent in 29% of human uLMS, most plausibly through promoter methylation.
caveats: Genetically engineered mouse tumours are not identical to human uLMS, and the 29% BRCA1-negative figure is IHC-based rather than an HRD score. Still the clearest lineage-matched argument that an HR-directed branch is worth testing on tissue.

intervention_label: PARP inhibition in HR-deficient uterine leiomyosarcoma PDX
model_system: uterine leiomyosarcoma patient-derived xenografts, including a paired post-PARPi-resistant PDX; national cohort screened by WGS/WES/panel
n_units: 58 individuals screened; 5 (9%) HRD; 13 samples by WGS
control_arm: olaparib alone and olaparib plus cisplatin as comparators to the PARP1-selective agent
dose_and_schedule: AZD5305 (PARP1-selective) vs olaparib vs olaparib+cisplatin in PDX
mechanism: synthetic lethality of PARP inhibition in tumours with biallelic HR-gene loss; PARP1-selective trapping as the more complete version of that mechanism
key_finding: Five of 58 uLMS (9%) were HR-deficient, all through homozygous BRCA2 deletion, and all 13 WGS samples carried a dominant COSMIC signature 3. PDX responses were fastest and most sustained with the PARP1-selective AZD5305, including in a paired PDX that had acquired PRKDC resistance mutations after patient PARPi exposure.
caveats: The responding models were biallelic BRCA2-deleted, a state this patient has not been tested for; signature 3 was near-universal but CHORD scores were high in only 2 of 13, so genome-wide LOH alone did not equal functional HRD.

intervention_label: PARP trapping as the reason olaparib pairs with temozolomide
model_system: isogenic DT40 and human cell lines with defined DNA-repair deletions; PARP inhibitors compared for trapping versus catalytic potency
control_arm: PARP1/2-null cells; catalytic-only inhibitor (veliparib) comparator
mechanism: temozolomide-induced N-methylpurine lesions generate base-excision-repair intermediates that trapped PARP-DNA complexes convert into cytotoxic replication blocks
key_finding: Synergy with temozolomide tracked with a drug's ability to trap PARP on DNA rather than with catalytic inhibition, so trapping-potent inhibitors combined far better than veliparib. Camptothecin combinations followed the same rule.
caveats: Engineered cell lines rather than sarcoma models. Explains why the olaparib-plus-temozolomide regimen is a mechanistic pairing rather than an empirical one.

intervention_label: PARP inhibitor plus temozolomide across paediatric solid-tumour xenografts
model_system: Pediatric Preclinical Testing Program xenograft panel including Ewing sarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma and osteosarcoma
control_arm: talazoparib alone, temozolomide alone, vehicle
dose_and_schedule: talazoparib (BMN 673) with temozolomide on the PPTP schedule
mechanism: PARP trapping potentiating temozolomide-induced base damage in vivo
key_finding: Talazoparib alone was largely inactive, while the combination with temozolomide produced objective regressions in a subset of xenografts, most consistently Ewing sarcoma. Myelosuppression forced temozolomide dose reduction in the combination.
caveats: No leiomyosarcoma model in the panel, and the responsive histology (Ewing) has a distinct DNA-damage biology. The haematologic toxicity signal is the part that carries directly into clinic.

intervention_label: ALT prevalence and ATRX loss in leiomyosarcoma
model_system: 92 human leiomyosarcomas (uterine, retroperitoneal and other sites) by telomere FISH, ATRX/DAXX IHC and TERT promoter sequencing
control_arm: ALT-negative tumours within the same series
mechanism: ATRX inactivation permits the recombination-based telomere maintenance that defines ALT
key_finding: ALT was present in 59% of leiomyosarcomas and ATRX expression was lost in 33%, with all but two ATRX-deficient tumours being ALT-positive. Both features went with epithelioid or pleomorphic morphology, necrosis and worse outcome.
caveats: Human tissue survey with no therapeutic arm. Sets a realistic pre-test probability that this tumour is ALT-positive, which matters only if an ALT-directed strategy has a real preclinical basis.

intervention_label: ATR inhibition in ALT-positive cells — the original claim
model_system: ALT-positive and telomerase-positive human cancer cell lines, including ATRX-deficient lines
control_arm: isogenic and matched telomerase-positive lines
mechanism: ALT depends on ATR-coordinated homologous recombination at telomeres, so ATR inhibition disrupts telomere maintenance selectively
key_finding: ALT-positive lines were selectively killed by ATR inhibitors while telomerase-positive lines were spared, and ATRX loss was linked to the ALT phenotype.
caveats: In-vitro only, and the selectivity claim failed to replicate in later work — read alongside Deeg 2016 and Goncalves 2020 rather than on its own.

intervention_label: ALT cells are not generally hypersensitive to ATR inhibition — failed replication
model_system: panel of ALT-positive and telomerase-positive cell lines including U2OS and ALT-positive glioma lines
control_arm: telomerase-positive lines; multiple ATR inhibitors
mechanism: direct test of whether the ALT phenotype itself confers ATR dependency
key_finding: Across a broader panel and several ATR inhibitors, ALT-positive lines showed no general hypersensitivity relative to telomerase-positive lines.
caveats: Contradicts Flynn 2015. In-vitro only, but the negative result is the reason ALT status alone should not be treated as an ATR-inhibitor selection biomarker in this case.

intervention_label: ATR inhibition plus gemcitabine in soft-tissue sarcoma, independent of ALT
model_system: soft-tissue sarcoma cell lines and an undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma patient-derived xenograft
control_arm: single-agent VE-822, single-agent gemcitabine, vehicle
dose_and_schedule: VE-822 combined with gemcitabine in vitro and in vivo
mechanism: ATR inhibition removes the intra-S-phase checkpoint that would otherwise let cells survive gemcitabine-induced replication stress
key_finding: The VE-822 and gemcitabine combination was synergistic in vitro with increased gammaH2AX and S-phase accumulation, and in vivo it improved tumour growth inhibition and progression-free survival over either agent. Sensitivity did not track ALT status.
caveats: The in-vivo model was undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma, not leiomyosarcoma. Supports ATR inhibition as a chemo-sensitiser rather than as an ALT-selected strategy.

intervention_label: Telomere length, not ALT status, tracked ATR-inhibitor sensitivity
model_system: osteosarcoma cell lines of varying telomere length and telomere-maintenance mechanism
control_arm: long-telomere lines within the same panel
mechanism: short telomeres, rather than the recombination-based maintenance mechanism itself, create the ATR dependency
key_finding: ATR inhibitors selectively eliminated osteosarcoma lines with short telomeres regardless of whether those lines used ALT.
caveats: Osteosarcoma lines, in vitro. Reframes the biomarker as telomere length, which nobody has measured in this patient either.

intervention_label: MAGE-A4, PRAME and NY-ESO-1 prevalence across bone and soft-tissue sarcoma
model_system: human sarcoma specimens by IHC and multiplex immunostaining microarray; 26 smooth-muscle sarcomas among 128 tumours
n_units: n=128 (21 UPS, 26 smooth-muscle sarcoma, 28 liposarcoma, 40 osteosarcoma, 13 chondrosarcoma)
control_arm: cross-subtype comparison; testis as the reference positive tissue for this antigen class
mechanism: cancer/testis antigen expression as the second gate for HLA-restricted TCR and ImmTAC programs
key_finding: Expression was subtype-dependent, highest for MAGE-A4 and PRAME in UPS and osteosarcoma. NY-ESO-1 was low across every subtype, and the smooth-muscle sarcoma group was positive for MAGE-A4 in a minority of cases.
caveats: The reported MAGE-A4 percentages for smooth-muscle sarcoma are internally inconsistent between the results text and its own framing, and an erratum was issued (Cancer Med 2025;14:e70971) — treat the exact figure as soft. Smooth-muscle sarcoma here is not uterus-restricted.

intervention_label: Promoter demethylation as the switch that turns on MAGE genes
journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
model_system: 20 human tumour cell lines plus primary fibroblasts; CpG methylation mapping and 5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine treatment
control_arm: MAGE-1-negative lines; untreated fibroblasts
mechanism: CpG demethylation at Ets-binding sites in the MAGE-1 promoter permits transcription-factor binding, downstream of genome-wide demethylation in the tumour
key_finding: MAGE-1 promoter CpGs were demethylated in expressing lines and methylated in non-expressing ones, and 5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine switched the gene on even in normal fibroblasts. Overall CpG methylation was inversely correlated with MAGE-1 expression across the 20 lines.
caveats: MAGE-1 rather than MAGE-A4, and the work predates modern epigenomics. It is the reason cancer/testis antigen expression is patchy and epigenetically labile rather than a fixed lineage property — which is the honest answer to whether expression is stable enough for a TCR-T strategy.

intervention_label: Allele-specific HLA loss as an immune-escape route
model_system: multiregion whole-exome sequencing of primary non-small-cell lung tumours (TRACERx) with an HLA-specific LOH caller
n_units: LOH at the HLA locus in 40% of tumours analysed
control_arm: HLA-intact regions within the same tumours
mechanism: somatic loss of one HLA haplotype removes the restriction element without touching the antigen, under immune-editing selection
key_finding: HLA LOH occurred in around 40% of tumours, was frequently subclonal and enriched in metastatic or later subclones, and associated with a higher neoantigen burden in the affected regions.
caveats: Lung cancer under endogenous T-cell pressure, not sarcoma under engineered T cells. The relevance is that germline HLA-A*02:01 typing does not guarantee the pulmonary metastases still present that allele.

intervention_label: ADP-A2M4 (afamitresgene) affinity-enhanced MAGE-A4 TCR — preclinical potency and specificity
model_system: 2D and 3D human cell cultures, primary tumour material, and human primary-cell and cell-line cross-reactivity panels
control_arm: non-transduced T cells; HLA-A2-negative and MAGE-A4-negative targets
mechanism: affinity-enhanced TCR recognising the HLA-A*02-restricted MAGE-A4 peptide GVYDGREHTV on the tumour cell surface
key_finding: ADP-A2M4 killed MAGE-A4-positive HLA-A2-positive targets potently across 2D, 3D and primary tumour material. Alanine-scanning and primary-cell screening turned up no major off-target cross-reactivity.
caveats: Adaptimmune-authored; the tumour material tested was not uterine leiomyosarcoma. Potency is contingent on antigen expression, which is exactly what has not been measured in this patient.

intervention_label: Titin cross-reactivity of an affinity-enhanced MAGE-A3 TCR — the class safety lesson
model_system: in-vitro functional analysis of an affinity-enhanced HLA-A*01-restricted MAGE-A3 TCR; post-hoc amino-acid scanning and beating-cardiomyocyte cultures
control_arm: pre-SAE preclinical panels that had returned clean
mechanism: affinity enhancement broadens peptide tolerance, so a structurally similar peptide from a muscle protein becomes a target
key_finding: Conventional preclinical screening found no off-target activity, yet the engineered T cells caused fatal cardiac toxicity in patients. Amino-acid scanning afterwards identified the titin peptide ESDPIVAQY as the cross-reactive target.
caveats: A different TCR, a different antigen and a different HLA allele from the MAGE-A4 A*02:01 products in scope here. Logged because it is why the peptide-scanning and primary-cell work in the MAGE-A4 package matters, and because the off-target was a sarcomeric muscle protein.

intervention_label: MAGE-A4-specific TCR-NK cells against solid tumours
exclusion_reason: Allogeneic TCR-transduced NK-cell construct rather than either autologous TCR-T product in this case's trial set; the effector biology and the manufacturing constraints both differ enough that it does not inform the afami-cel or lete-cel decision.

intervention_label: PRAME/HLA-A2 epitope density and the immunoproteasome
model_system: PRAME-positive HLA-A2-positive human cancer and leukemia lines; mouse xenograft models of human leukemia; TCR-mimic antibody Pr20
control_arm: PRAME-negative and HLA-A2-negative lines; unmodified IgG
mechanism: the PRAME300-309 ALYVDSLFFL peptide is presented on HLA-A*02:01 at very low copy number, and immunoproteasome subunit beta5i induction after IFN-gamma raises the amount presented
key_finding: Surface PRAME/HLA-A2 complexes were present at ultra-low density, and an afucosylated TCR-mimic antibody was nonetheless therapeutically active against leukemia xenografts. IFN-gamma markedly increased Pr20 binding in some tumours by shifting proteasome cleavage away from destroying the epitope.
caveats: Leukemia and melanoma models, and a TCR-mimic antibody rather than a TCR-T or ImmTAC. The transferable point is that PRAME protein positivity by IHC and PRAME epitope density on HLA-A2 are not the same quantity.

intervention_label: PRAME as a dominant repressor of retinoic-acid receptor signalling
model_system: human melanoma and other cancer lines with PRAME knockdown; in-vitro and in-vivo proliferation assays
control_arm: control shRNA; PRAME-low lines
mechanism: PRAME binds liganded RAR and recruits Polycomb proteins to RAR target promoters, blocking retinoic-acid-induced differentiation and growth arrest
key_finding: PRAME knockdown restored RAR signalling in RA-resistant melanoma and reinstated sensitivity to retinoic acid in vitro and in vivo.
caveats: Melanoma, no sarcoma model. Relevant to the antigen-stability question: PRAME appears to be functionally selected for in the tumour rather than being inert cargo, which argues against easy antigen-loss escape but does not prove it.

intervention_label: PRAME-directed mTCR-CAR T cells in acute myeloid leukemia
exclusion_reason: Model system is AML, where PRAME expression, antigen density and effector access all differ from a solid mesenchymal tumour; contributes nothing on the sarcoma question that Chang 2017 does not cover better.

intervention_label: Sarcoma immune classes and B-cell-rich tertiary lymphoid structures
model_system: gene-expression profiling of 608 soft-tissue sarcomas with validation against a phase 2 pembrolizumab cohort
control_arm: cross-class comparison within the same cohort
mechanism: composition of the tumour microenvironment, and specifically B-cell-rich tertiary lymphoid structures, governs whether PD-1 blockade has anything to act on
key_finding: Five immune phenotypes emerged, from immune-low (A, B) to immune-high (D, E). Class E, defined by tertiary lymphoid structures rich in B cells and follicular dendritic cells, had better survival and a high response rate to pembrolizumab, and B-cell content outperformed CD8 content as a predictor.
caveats: Leiomyosarcoma sits predominantly in the immune-low classes, which is the structural reason single-agent checkpoint blockade underperforms in this histology. Class assignment requires an expression assay nobody has run here.

intervention_label: Single-cell map of the metastatic uterine leiomyosarcoma microenvironment
model_system: single-cell RNA sequencing of metastatic lesions from one treatment-naive uterine leiomyosarcoma patient versus normal myometrium
n_units: 1 uLMS patient (4 metastatic sites); n=5 normal myometrium
control_arm: normal uterine myometrium
mechanism: exhausted CD8 T cells, M2-polarised tumour-associated macrophages and immature N2 neutrophils together with MIF-CD74/CD44 and CXCL8 signalling produce an immunosuppressed niche
key_finding: Metastatic uLMS lesions were dominated by exhausted CD8 T cells, CD163-positive M2 macrophages and CD15-positive immature neutrophils, with naive markers lost along the pseudotime trajectory. CXCL8 signalling linked angiogenesis to macrophage polarisation in the same niche.
caveats: A single patient's metastases, so cell-type frequencies are anecdotal even if the qualitative picture matches the wider literature. No therapeutic arm.

intervention_label: PI3K/mTOR inhibition sensitising pS6-high uterine leiomyosarcoma to PD-1 blockade
model_system: humanized and immunodeficient uterine leiomyosarcoma patient-derived xenografts; TCGA analysis of 101 LMS; serial single-cell RNA/TCR sequencing of biopsies
control_arm: single-agent anti-PD-1, single-agent PI3K/mTOR inhibitor, vehicle
dose_and_schedule: PI3K/mTOR inhibitor with anti-PD-1 in a humanized uLMS PDX
mechanism: PI3K/mTOR overactivation associates with lymphocyte depletion; inhibiting it repolarises macrophages, raises antigen presentation on dendritic and tumour cells, and draws in PD-1-positive T cells that then need checkpoint release
key_finding: Single-agent anti-PD-1 produced no response in the ICB-resistant humanized uLMS PDX, while combining it with PI3K/mTOR inhibition gave partial or complete responses. The combination reinvigorated exhausted T cells and drove clonal expansion of a cytotoxic CD8 population supported by CD4 Th1 cells.
caveats: Humanized PDX immunology is an approximation of a human immune system, and the pS6-high selection marker has not been measured in this patient. The nearest lineage-matched argument that checkpoint blockade in uLMS needs a partner rather than a companion diagnostic.

intervention_label: Antiangiogenic plus anti-PD-L1 therapy and high endothelial venule formation
model_system: mouse models of pancreatic neuroendocrine tumour, mammary carcinoma and glioblastoma
control_arm: single-agent anti-VEGFR2, single-agent anti-PD-L1, vehicle
mechanism: VEGF blockade normalises tumour vasculature and induces high endothelial venules, which in turn permit cytotoxic T-cell entry that checkpoint blockade can then sustain
key_finding: The combination prolonged survival and produced tumour regression in models where either agent alone did little, and the benefit tracked with intratumoural high endothelial venule formation and increased CTL infiltration. Anti-PD-L1 also sustained vessel normalisation, making the interaction reciprocal.
caveats: Carcinoma and neuroendocrine models, no sarcoma. This is the mechanistic ancestor of the PD-1 x VEGF bispecific rationale rather than evidence about ivonescimab itself.

intervention_label: Ivonescimab tetravalent PD-1 x VEGF bispecific — cooperative binding and Fc silencing
model_system: biophysical and cell-based assays plus mouse tumour models; cynomolgus monkey safety
control_arm: parental anti-PD-1 and anti-VEGF antibodies and their combination
mechanism: VEGF dimers cross-link the tetravalent antibody into soluble complexes that raise its avidity for PD-1, and PD-1 engagement reciprocally strengthens VEGF binding; Fc mutations abrogate FcgammaRI/IIIa binding
key_finding: Each target enhanced binding to the other, so PD-1/PD-L1 and VEGF blockade were both more potent than with the separate antibodies. Fc silencing cut effector function in vitro, consistent with the tolerability seen in monkeys and patients, and the antibody produced a significant in-vivo antitumor response.
caveats: Authored entirely by the sponsor, and the in-vivo work is in humanized-mouse tumour models with no sarcoma among them. Explains the molecular design; says nothing about leiomyosarcoma.

intervention_label: B7-H3 expression across soft-tissue sarcoma subtypes
model_system: 153 human soft-tissue sarcoma specimens across 15 subtypes, scored by IHC for tumour and vessel staining
control_arm: within-cohort comparison; PD-L1/PD-1 status where previously assessed
mechanism: B7-H3 surface expression as the antigen available to an ADC or a T-cell engager
key_finding: B7-H3 was expressed in 97% of samples and at high level in 69.2%, with vessel positivity in 94.7%. Expression was independent of prior treatment, tumour size, grade, age, and of PD-L1 or PD-1 status.
caveats: Prevalence, not density in molecules per cell, which is the quantity that actually governs CAR and ADC activity. Leiomyosarcoma is one of 15 subtypes in the cohort rather than the focus.

intervention_label: B7-H3 CAR T cells and the antigen-density threshold
model_system: xenograft models of osteosarcoma, medulloblastoma and Ewing sarcoma; target lines titrated for surface B7-H3
control_arm: untransduced T cells; antigen-low and antigen-negative target lines
mechanism: CAR engagement scales with surface antigen copy number, so a density threshold separates tumour killing from sparing of low-expressing normal tissue
key_finding: B7-H3 CAR T cells regressed established solid-tumour xenografts, and efficacy depended heavily on high surface antigen density. Activity fell away sharply against low-expressing targets, which is what creates the therapeutic window over normal tissue.
caveats: Paediatric tumour xenografts, no leiomyosarcoma. The density-threshold result is the reason a 'B7-H3 positive' IHC call is insufficient on its own for a CAR strategy, and it applies with less force to an ADC with a bystander payload.

intervention_label: Vobramitamab duocarmazine in B7-H3-expressing neuroblastoma models
model_system: neuroblastoma cell lines and orthotopic/metastatic mouse xenograft models with varying B7-H3 levels
control_arm: isotype-ADC control; untreated mice
dose_and_schedule: vobramitamab duocarmazine (MGC018) administered intravenously in xenograft-bearing mice
mechanism: B7-H3-directed antibody delivering a duocarmycin payload, with membrane-permeable released drug killing neighbouring antigen-low cells
key_finding: The ADC inhibited tumour growth and extended survival across models, with activity extending to cells expressing lower B7-H3 through bystander killing of adjacent cells.
caveats: Neuroblastoma only, and the payload class differs from the topoisomerase-I payloads carried by the B7-H3 ADCs in this case's trial set. The bystander principle is what transfers, not the potency numbers.

intervention_label: CC-3, a B7-H3 x CD3 bispecific antibody, against bone and soft-tissue sarcoma
model_system: sarcoma cell lines of multiple subtypes with healthy-donor T cells; patient sarcoma specimens for expression and outcome
control_arm: B7-H3-negative target cells; control bispecific/T cells alone
mechanism: IgG-based B7-H3 x CD3 bispecific redirects polyclonal T cells to B7-H3-positive tumour cells independent of TCR specificity or HLA
key_finding: B7-H3 was found on every sarcoma line tested, and CC-3 triggered T-cell activation, cytokine release, proliferation, memory differentiation and target-restricted lysis. Higher B7-H3 in patient specimens went with shorter progression-free and overall survival.
caveats: In-vitro only — no xenograft arm — and the sarcoma line panel is not leiomyosarcoma-specific. HLA-independence is the practical contrast with the TCR-T options in this case.

intervention_label: B7-H3 overexpression in osteosarcoma
exclusion_reason: Osteosarcoma-only expression survey, superseded for this case by the 153-patient soft-tissue sarcoma series (Lynch 2024) that includes leiomyosarcoma and reports vessel staining as well.

intervention_label: Trabectedin's selective depletion of mononuclear phagocytes
model_system: four mouse tumour models with myeloid-cell transfer and depletion experiments; trabectedin-resistant tumour cells; blood and tumour from treated patients
control_arm: untreated tumour-bearing mice; trabectedin-resistant tumour cells to separate direct from myeloid effects
mechanism: caspase-8-dependent apoptosis restricted to mononuclear phagocytes, with selectivity over neutrophils and lymphocytes set by differential signalling and decoy TRAIL receptor expression
key_finding: Trabectedin depleted monocytes and macrophages from blood, spleen and tumour across four mouse models, with angiogenesis falling alongside. Transfer and depletion experiments using trabectedin-resistant tumour cells established that killing mononuclear phagocytes is a real component of the antitumour effect, and monocyte depletion was reproduced in treated patients.
caveats: None of the four mouse models is uterine leiomyosarcoma. Directly relevant here because the metastatic uLMS niche is macrophage-rich, which makes the planned first-line agent partly an immune-modulating one.

intervention_label: Transcription-coupled repair and VHL-dependent RNA polymerase II degradation after trabectedin
model_system: human cell lines with defined defects in transcription-coupled nucleotide excision repair and in VHL
control_arm: TC-NER-proficient and VHL-proficient isogenic lines
mechanism: trabectedin-DNA adducts stall elongating RNA polymerase II, and degradation of the stalled polymerase requires both transcription-coupled NER and VHL
key_finding: Trabectedin caused rapid RNA polymerase II degradation that depended on both TC-NER and VHL, tying cytotoxicity to transcription rather than to replication alone.
caveats: Isogenic human cell lines, no tumour model. Explains why trabectedin is a transcription-targeted drug and why repair-pathway status, not proliferation rate, is where a predictive biomarker would sit.

intervention_label: ET-743 activity across cells with defined DNA-repair defects
model_system: yeast and mammalian cell panels with defined NER, mismatch-repair, DNA-PK and ATM deficiencies
control_arm: repair-proficient parental lines and complemented revertants
mechanism: NER machinery converts the minor-groove adduct into a lethal lesion, while double-strand-break repair capacity determines how well the cell survives it
key_finding: NER-deficient lines were 2- to 8-fold less sensitive to ET-743 and restoring NER re-sensitised them, the opposite of the usual pattern for DNA-damaging drugs. Cells lacking DNA-PK or ATM were more sensitive, and mismatch-repair status made no difference.
caveats: Engineered cell systems from 2001, no tumour model. The closest thing to a mechanistic biomarker of trabectedin benefit: intact NER plus impaired double-strand-break repair, which is the profile an HR-deficient uLMS would have.

intervention_label: NER and homologous-recombination cross-talk in trabectedin's mechanism
exclusion_reason: Mechanism worked out entirely in fission yeast with rad13 mutants; the mammalian version of the same NER-dependence and HR-repair claim is covered by Damia 2001 and Aune 2008 without the species gap.

intervention_label: ET-743 combined with doxorubicin in sarcoma models
model_system: TE-671 rhabdomyosarcoma xenografts in nude mice; UV2237M murine fibrosarcoma and its doxorubicin-resistant Pgp-overexpressing subline
control_arm: single-agent ET-743, single-agent doxorubicin, untreated controls
dose_and_schedule: ET-743 and doxorubicin simultaneously, or ET-743 1 h before doxorubicin, or the reverse sequence
mechanism: a transcription-targeted minor-groove binder combined with a topoisomerase II poison, hitting non-overlapping lesions
key_finding: Isobologram analysis showed an additive interaction with combination indices slightly below 1. In TE-671 xenografts each drug alone was marginal (log cell kill 0.13 and 0.33) while the combination reached 0.85 to 1.12, best when ET-743 preceded doxorubicin by an hour, and no pharmacokinetic interaction was found.
caveats: Pre-dates the LMS-04 regimen by nearly two decades and neither model is leiomyosarcoma. The interaction was additive rather than synergistic, and in the fibrosarcoma lung-metastasis arm the combination did not beat either drug alone.

intervention_label: Histone eviction as a second mechanism of anthracycline action
model_system: human cancer cell lines, mouse tissues including heart, and primary AML blasts from patients
control_arm: etoposide and doxorubicin variants that break DNA without evicting histones
mechanism: anthracyclines evict histones, including H2AX, from open chromatin independently of double-strand-break formation, which deregulates transcription and blunts the damage response
key_finding: Doxorubicin evicted histones from open chromatin whether or not it induced double-strand breaks, and H2AX eviction was accompanied by attenuated DNA repair. The same eviction happened in heart tissue and could kill topoisomerase-negative AML blasts.
caveats: No sarcoma model. Matters here for two reasons: it explains anthracycline activity in slowly proliferating tumours, and it links the same mechanism to cardiac tissue in a patient whose baseline LVEF has not yet been measured.
